scripts.comment: It can be argued that Scratch (from which we inherited ASK AND WAIT) should have implemented this as the primitive for interaction in the first place. We won't speculate about why they chose to do what they did, but we've thought about making this change in Snap!. ANSWER TO PROMPT is simpler because you see the prompt in the code at the point where you're using the answer, rather than having to look back in the code to find what the question was.

scripts.comment: Students may wonder if ASK NAME calling ANSWER TO PROMPT isn't overdoing the abstraction here; why not just call ANSWER TO PROMPT three times for the three inputs to the CONTACT WITH block? One answer is that so far our data structure is overly simple. ASK NAME should really ask for first name and last name; ASK ADDRESS should ask for street address, city, state, zip, country. So these procedures will be more than the simple one-liners they are now, calling ANSWER TO PROMPT more than once.
The variable SAMPLE CONTACT LIST contains the example in the text, in case you erase the main CONTACT LIST variable.
